author: vivekananda
period: Written and delivered in the mid-1890s; published around 1896
summary: Vivekananda's account of the path of devotion, from preparatory worship to supreme love for God.
whyRead: It draws on classical bhakti sources and Ramanuja while framing devotion in terms accessible to a modern audience. It is a modern exposition, not a classical text.
questions: Is love of God compatible with non-dual knowledge?

keyTeachings.title: Two stages
keyTeachings.text: Devotion is divided into preparatory devotion (gauni), involving symbols, images and ritual, and supreme devotion (para), in which love for God becomes spontaneous.

keyTeachings.title: The need for a teacher
keyTeachings.text: He stresses the qualities of a true teacher and student and the transmission of spiritual force.

keyTeachings.title: Love as its own reward
keyTeachings.text: Supreme devotion is love for its own sake, seeking nothing in return, and it naturally brings renunciation.

structure.label: A short book in two parts
structure.note: Preparatory and supreme devotion; contents vary slightly between editions

relatedTexts.note: A classical source for its account of supreme love
